- id: '1'
  proposal:
    quote: the result bears on whether the claim is integrated into the working theory and causally useful there
    change: 'Keep "fit" throughout and replace the ordinary word "integration" for the same thing: "bears on whether the claim fits the working theory and is causally useful there" (paragraph 1), and "System-building consequences are real evidence for fit and causal usefulness" (paragraph 6). Two replacements.'
    reason: 'The note names one thing two ways: "fit" in the title, description, paragraph 2 ("System use primarily exposes fit", "operative fit") and Scope ("theory fit"), and "integrated"/"integration" in paragraphs 1 and 6. A reader can take these as two referents. The deciding occurrence for keeping "fit" is "System use primarily exposes fit", which rests on the linked definition in "A claim''s test record does not determine its fit in a working theory" (relevance, scope, agreement with retained claims, changed decisions). "Integration" would lose that content. The paragraph 6 sentence is in `defend`; the swap aligns it with the title''s "theory fit and causal usefulness" and does not narrow it, but the operator may prefer to leave the defended sentence verbatim and change paragraph 1 only.'
  state: approved

- id: '2'
  proposal:
    quote: Read-back must assign the failure at the granularity the evidence supports
    change: 'Replace the term with the ordinary words: "Interpreting the outcome must assign the failure at the granularity the evidence supports rather than treating every bad outcome as a refutation of the theory." One replacement.'
    reason: '"Read-back" occurs once, without a definition or link. Elsewhere in the KB it names retrieving retained memory into a later decision (e.g. the agentic-system memory reviews and read-back-mechanisms comparison), so here it reads as a collision. In this sentence it means interpreting a system-use outcome and assigning blame; the ordinary words carry the claim without widening or narrowing it. No occurrence needs the distinction.'
